LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponRatings_Tip: A rating from 1 to 10 for every weapon, from what it really does in a fight by the game's own rules, with its sub-ratings, colour-coded tags and a line in plain words, at the top of the game's info card. Off, no weapon is rated anywhere.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponCard_Tip: Rimfolk's own card for a weapon: the tags as chips, a chart of damage by distance and armour, the situations, the effects, the key numbers, and the rating for one colonist with why it differs, against what they hold and carry (Simple Sidearms, Dual Wield, RunAndGun and Melee Animation where loaded). Opens from the info card, the gear tab and a button on a weapon on the map.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_WeaponCard: A button on the info card, the gear tab and a selected weapon opens Rimfolk's card for it.
LanguageData.CC_Weapon_Info_RatingExpl: How much this weapon gets done in the fights it is made for, from 1 to 10, worked out by the game's own rules: the chance to hit at each distance, armour against its piercing, warm-up, burst and cooldown, its blasts, fire, stuns and EMP, what it does to whoever holds it and the abilities it grants. Guns, bows and launchers share one scale and melee weapons another; 5.5 is the middle, about an assault rifle or a steel longsword. A point up near the middle is about a third more damage dealt for a gun and a fifth more for a melee weapon.
LanguageData.CC_Weapon_Info_RatedAs: Judged as {ROLE}, for a colonist of {SKILL} 8 with no traits, against the enemies a colony meets after its first year: raiders in plain clothes, in flak and in marine armour, and mechanoids.
LanguageData.CC_Weapon_Info_Rough: Read roughly: part of what it does can't be valued, so it is rated on the rest. Why:
LanguageData.CC_Weapon_Info_PlainExpl: The weapon as a seasoned player would sum it up, made from its rating and its tags.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponCardFirst_Tip: Opening the info for a weapon (the "i" button on the gear tab, Nice Inventory Tab, a trade screen, a list, the research or architect tab, the inspect pane) opens Rimfolk's weapon card instead of the game's. Its button "All the game's stats" opens the game's card, and the game's card keeps its button back. Links followed inside the game's card stay in it. Off, the game's card opens as before.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_WeaponCardFirst: A weapon's info opens as Rimfolk's weapon card; the game's card is one button away.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponSuggestions_Tip: The best weapon for each colonist from what the colony has, by their skill, traits, passions and work, their faith, the weapon mods and the fights you meet, with why in a line: on the gear tab (a row in Nice Inventory Tab's equipment box, or under the game's list) with a button to equip it, on a weapon's card (who should carry it), and for the whole colony on the Defenses page, where "Equip all suggested" gives the orders. Two colonists are never told to take the same weapon, and a trade between two is suggested when it is better for both, or when the colony gains clearly by putting the better weapon in the hands of the one who fights more. A lucky weapon or an heirloom given up is always said, never a bar.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_WeaponSuggestions: The gear tab, a weapon's card and the Defenses page suggest a better weapon from the colony's stores.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponAsks_Tip: Now and then a colonist says in one line that a clearly better weapon lying in storage would suit them, naming it and why, or proposes a trade to another colonist once the two are together (the one who would gain asks, the one who rarely fights offers theirs), in their free time at home: at most once in five days each and once a day in the colony, and not while you have set their suggestions aside. Nobody offers up their own lucky weapon or heirloom. A quiet entry stays in This week while it still stands.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_WeaponAsks: Colonists sometimes ask for a clearly better weapon they've seen in storage, or propose a trade.

Off, nothing shows until there is something to suggest.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_WeaponKitSelf_Tip: With Simple Sidearms every colonist who can fight should carry one ranged and one melee weapon, and with Dual Wield a weapon in the off hand where their hands and the weapons allow it. A colonist with an empty slot goes, in their free time at home and safe, and takes a fitting weapon from storage: into an empty hand, as a sidearm, or into the off hand, by the game's and the mods' own jobs; a weapon already in their pack is kept as a sidearm. Only empty slots, never in place of a weapon they hold; never a forbidden weapon (they may ask for it); at most once a day each, with a line as they take it. Off, an empty slot is only suggested, and colonists ask for it now and then.
